To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the signaling lymphocyte activation molecule‐associated protein (SLAM‐associated) protein is required for invariant NKT (iNK) T cell differentiation and that the lack of this protein leads to the development of iNK17 over iNK2 cells.
SLAM‐associated protein (SLAMAP) is essential not only for IL4 production but also the terminal differentiation of iNK T2 cells.
SLAM‐associated protein (SLAMAP) is essential to promote the development of iNKt2 cells and to prevent the emergence of iNKt17 cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of signaling lymphocyte activation molecule‐associated protein (SLAM‐associated) in the development and differentiation of invariant NKT cells (iNKT).
the role of SAP in the terminal differentiation of iNK T cells.
the role of SAP in thymocyte development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SAP is essential for the differentiation of iNKt2 cells, while it is not required for the development of iNKt17 cells.
SAP is required for the terminal differentiation and function of iNKT cells, and that its loss leads to an expansion of iNKT‐17‐like cells.
SAP favors the development of IL‐4+ iNKT2 and iNKT1 cells at the expense of IL‐17+ iNKT17 and IFN‐γ+ iNKT1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SLAM‐associated protein (encoded by SH2D1A gene) is essential for the development of invariant natural killer T (iNKT2) over iNKT1 and iNKT17 subsets.
SAP is a master regulator for iNKT2 cell development and function.
SAP is a critical factor for the development of i‐NKT2 over the iNKT17 cell lineage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SLAM‐associated protein is essential to the development of IL‐4 producing invariant natural killer T (iNKT2) cells.
SAP is a critical regulator of iNKT lineage commitment.
SAP is not only required for the development of all iNKT cell lineages, but is also essential for the terminal differentiation into iNKT2 and iNKT17 subsets.
